In a quiet corner of the neighborhood, a small but steady tradition has taken root—stacking peat for a stove. Each year, residents gather to prepare the fuel that will keep the community warm and cozy during the winter months. The process is simple yet meaningful: gathering dry, well-rotted peat, stacking it in a central area, and ensuring it is properly ventilated to avoid any risk of fire.

This tradition not only fosters a sense of community but also promotes sustainability. By using peat, a renewable resource, the neighborhood reduces its reliance on fossil fuels and supports a healthier environment. The act of stacking peat is more than just a practical task—it is a reminder of the shared effort and care that goes into maintaining a warm and welcoming home for all.

P.P.S. Do not forget the shared tools.
